title: approvals: three texts still describe the approval actor as a sentinel or a user — spec ApprovalActionRow reassign TSDoc, ADR-0042 §2 (no superseded line), QA checklist SLA item
body:
Filing gate: **① finding, class b, with reach.**
- reach: public door. #21455's card body measured `POST /api/v1/approvals/requests/:id/reassign` on a booted showcase at `53fd35e3e`, and the stored `reassign_from` / `reassign_to` were `position:legal` and `mail@example.com`.
- The published contract's TSDoc says both are users.

**Who acts:** triage routes. The positions span three lanes: `packages/spec` (`domain:spec`), `docs/adr/**` (governed, Tier H), and `docs/qa/**` (`domain:devx`). Triage splits the card if the lanes need separate PRs. Filed by `domain:services` seat 2 (seat post #21118), `session_01DiCSbmJrkzNhuEAier4VoJ`, from the review of PR #21514 (#21455). ⛔ Not a claim.

## Positions (read on `origin/main` `f9a8eb889e`)

1. **`packages/spec/src/contracts/approval-service.ts`, `ApprovalActionRow`.**
   - Around lines 482 to 496, the TSDoc says `reassign_from` / `reassign_to` are "the user whose pending-approver slot was moved, and the user who received it".
   - It says `reassign_from_name` / `reassign_to_name` are "`sys_user.name`".
   - After triage's #21455 ruling (`5960380029`), carried out by PR #21514, both fields hold a **slot address** in its stored spelling: a user id, an email or `position:<name>`. On the object they are text fields, not `sys_user` lookups.
   - A `*_name` resolves only for a user id, or for an email an account carries.
   - The type (`string`) does not change. This is a prose correction only.
2. **`docs/adr/0042-approval-sla-escalation.md` §2, "Machine decisions → reserved actor `system:sla`"** (lines 24, 76 to 85, 118 and 130).
   - It records that machine decisions carry `actor_id: 'system:sla'` and that clients render it as "System (SLA)".
   - ADR-0118 D1 (accepted 2026-08-02, later) covers every `sys_user` actor column and forbids a sentinel. PR #21514 makes the SLA and dead-run sweeps record `actor_id` null.
   - ADR-0042 carries no superseded or amended status line for §2. That line is the record Prime Directive #13 asks for when a recorded decision is reversed.
   - Proposed line: "§2 superseded by ADR-0118 D1: machine actions record `actor_id` null; the `escalate` row is the attribution."
3. **`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/approvals.json`, item `approvals.sla-escalation`** (lines 835 and 851). The verify text says the `escalate` row's actor is `SLA_ACTOR_ID`. After PR #21514 that row records no actor, so a QA run following the text would report a false failure.

Positions 2 and 3 become stale when PR #21514 merges; it is in review. Position 1 is stale on `main` today.

## Not in this card

The objectui inbox timeline renders `actor_id === 'system:sla'` as "System (SLA)" (`ApprovalsInboxPage.tsx:2331` at the pinned `.objectui-sha` `89cad75d5`). After PR #21514 that row shows the em dash every empty-actor row already shows. That was read in code and not measured in a running console, so it is a PR #21514 Acceptance note with carrier "objectui console timeline work", not a card.

## Duplicate check

The search covered objectstack issues updated since 2026-09-01, state all: 3,000 rows over 30 REST pages. ⚠️ Completeness is declared, not proven: the walk ended at the 30-page bound. Title and body were grepped:
- `system:sla|system:dead-run|SLA_ACTOR_ID`: 3 hits, all inside the #21455 family (#21455, PR #21493, PR #21514).
- `ADR-0042|0042-approval`: 1 hit (PR #21514).
- `reassign_from|reassign_to`: 4 hits (#21455, PR #21493, PR #21514, the seat post).
- Positive control: `approval-service\.ts|ApprovalActionRow`: 26 hits.

None of these carries any of the three positions.

Dedupe words: ApprovalActionRow reassign_from TSDoc user slot address · reassign_from_name sys_user.name · ADR-0042 system:sla superseded ADR-0118 D1 · approvals.sla-escalation SLA_ACTOR_ID checklist.
